name: La Casa de la Playa
positioning: All-suite hotel on a secluded stretch of the Riviera Maya coast just outside Playa del Carmen, filled with handcrafted Mexican art and design
best_for: Travelers who want a suite with its own plunge pool and butler-drawn baths
Guests who want included admission to the Grupo Xcaret parks and tours

facts.text: The hotel sits on a secluded stretch of the Riviera Maya coastline, about 45 minutes south of Cancun International Airport and just outside Playa del Carmen.
Architect David Quintana filled the property with handcrafted works by Mexican artisans, native materials and contemporary design rooted in its surroundings.
The suites are adorned with artwork and handcrafted pieces created by Mexican artisans, and they look out on views of nature.
Suite benefits include a volcanic stone bathtub.
The Beach Front Suite has ocean views and direct access to the beach.
The Master Suites have a spacious design and panoramic ocean views.
Admission to all of Grupo Xcaret's parks and tours is included in a stay.
At Tuch de Luna, Chef Martha Ortiz celebrates Mexican cuisine with an all-female team.
Xal, by chef Andoni Luis Aduriz, is inspired by the Manila Route, which connected Mexico, Asia and Europe for more than 250 years.

highlights.text: The oceanfront suites have a built-in jellyfish aquarium in the wall beside the bed.
A rooftop infinity pool looks out over the Caribbean, and a lower glass-walled infinity pool projects over the sea.
Each suite's outdoor space has a large plunge pool, a hammock, an oversized daybed and a soaking tub where butlers prepare custom baths with honey- or mint-infused products.
Muluk Spa has an ocean-view hydrotherapy ritual with a sauna, steam room and cold room.
Curated experiences include candlelit dinners inside cenotes after the Grupo Xcaret parks have closed and private expeditions through underground caves.

considerations.text: The shoreline is made up of rocky outcroppings rather than a long walkable beach, so the pools and the views are the focal point.
WhataHotel notes it is an adults-only property, not suited to families with children.
